evidence_quotes.agenda: 'Do you have any questions about your estimate or pricing?' — the closest analog to the agenda question, but asked near the end, after all logistics probing was already complete, and scoped narrowly to pricing rather than the whole move.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer, unprompted: 'I think I'm more worried about like the heavy books that might be a lot.' Rep followed up asking about bookshelf count and coached her to pack totes lighter — resolved to the customer's satisfaction.
evidence_quotes.save_your_ass: 'The biggest thing you can do is be prepared and reduce small floating items... the better you're getting everything in the boxes... the quicker your move will go.'

top_strength: Genuinely responsive to an unprompted worry about heavy book totes, with specific, practical packing advice rather than a generic reassurance — and took real ownership of a product-feedback point (online booking notes field not surfacing to reps).
coaching_note: Meet Your Mover and both Stage 2 takeaway items were skipped entirely, and the closest thing to an agenda question came in at the very end scoped only to pricing — moving a genuine 'anything else on your mind about this move?' check earlier would surface concerns sooner and open room for the missing differentiators.
grading_notes: Judgment calls: (1) stage1_their_agenda scored 4 (asked-after-probing) rather than 0, crediting the late 'questions about your estimate or pricing' line as a narrow analog to the formal agenda ask; (2) stage3_close scored full credit (5) as an already-booked confirmation call with no natural rate-lock/explicit-ask moment; (3) the '99 percent of moves have damages under $2,000' track-record line was credited as satisfying the SYA commit-to-rate/experience framing in spirit.
